results.name: psf__requests-2148
results.summary: Body-streaming errors are not translated: Response.iter_content's inner generate() generator catches only IncompleteRead (->ChunkedEncodingError) and DecodeError (->ContentDecodingError), so a raw socket.error raised by httplib/urllib3 while reading the response body propagates to callers unchanged (this also affects Response.content/text, which consume iter_content). adapters.py already handles socket.error at send-time (line 389-390, raising ConnectionError), but that path does not cover exceptions raised while streaming/consuming the body. The change: in requests/models.py add `import socket` and wrap the streaming read so that a bare socket.error is re-raised as requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, while preserving the existing IncompleteRead/DecodeError mappings and not double-wrapping ReadTimeoutError. Add ConnectionError to the models.py exceptions import (line 23-25). A regression test simulating a mid-stream socket reset belongs in tests/test_requests.py.

results.name: mwaskom__seaborn-3010
results.summary: PolyFit._fit_predict passes raw x/y (including None/NaN) directly into np.polyfit, np.linspace, and np.polyval, so missing values propagate into the least-squares solve and raise LinAlgError ('SVD did not converge'). GroupBy.apply does not drop NA before invoking the stat. The minimal fix is to filter non-finite x/y rows inside PolyFit._fit_predict before fitting (and before computing the grid), and to handle the insufficient-points case consistently with the existing x.nunique() <= order branch. A regression test asserting no exception and expected output shape/columns for missing data (with and without grouping) belongs alongside the existing TestPolyFit tests.

results.name: psf__requests-2674
results.summary: The urllib3 exception leak originates in the adapter's exception-conversion block and the response-stream generator. requests/adapters.py HTTPAdapter.send already converts ProtocolError/socket.error, MaxRetryError (ConnectTimeoutError->ConnectTimeout, ResponseError->RetryError), ProxyError, SSLError and ReadTimeoutError, but has no clause for a directly-raised urllib3 DecodeError or for the generic urllib3 TimeoutError (the proxy-timeout case); the generic TimeoutError clause must be ordered after the ReadTimeoutError/ConnectTimeoutError subclass clauses so they are not swallowed. requests/models.py Response.iter_content.generate() wraps ProtocolError->ChunkedEncodingError, DecodeError->ContentDecodingError and ReadTimeoutError->ConnectionError, but likewise does not convert a generic urllib3 TimeoutError raised during streaming. Regression tests belong in test_requests.py (existing ConnectTimeout wrapping tests around lines 1504-1512), and HISTORY.rst documents exception-wrapping behavior. Not modified (write mode disabled).

results.name: mwaskom__seaborn-2848
results.summary: The failure comes from PairGrid assuming every hue value in the data is represented in hue_order. In seaborn/axisgrid.py PairGrid.__init__ (hue branch around line 1281) `hue_names = hue_order = categorical_order(data[hue], hue_order)` stores the user-provided subset order while self.hue_vals keeps the full hue column, so downstream grouping/plotting (map_diag/_map_diag_iter_hue, _plot_bivariate) and _get_palette receive a hue vector containing levels absent from hue_order. The categorical_order helper (seaborn/_core/rules.py, line 125) returns a user order verbatim and its variable_type/unique path (line 149-150) can hit np.isnan on the full column. Fix by subsetting self.data to rows whose hue is in hue_order before computing categories/palette/masks, in PairGrid.__init__, and making categorical_order/legend construction honor the requested subset order consistently. Add a regression test in TestPairGrid (tests/test_axisgrid.py, class at line 677) asserting pairplot(iris, hue='species', hue_order=['setosa','versicolor']) runs without exception and yields exactly the requested legend levels.

results.name: psf__requests-863
results.summary: Localized the hooks parsing issue to requests/models.py. Request.__init__ (line ~151) loops over the hooks dict and calls self.register_hook(event=k, hook=v) with the raw value; register_hook (line ~463) unconditionally appends the value, so a list value becomes a nested list and later fails in dispatch_hook since list is not callable. The fix must normalize each value in Request.register_hook (append callables, extend non-string iterables) or add parsing in Request.__init__ before registering, while keeping single-callable behavior backward compatible. requests/hooks.py dispatch_hook already accepts lists and needs no change for accepted values, though its callable check precedence is relevant to the normalization rule. Session.request's setdefault-based merging in requests/sessions.py (line ~170) passes session hooks through unchanged, so no change is required there for flat lists. Tests test_multiple_hooks already covers list values in tests/test_requests.py (line ~713) and can be extended.

results.name: psf__requests-2317
results.summary: The bug is the method normalization at requests/sessions.py line 428 in Session.request: `method = builtin_str(method)`. On Python 3 builtin_str is `str`, so passing bytes (e.g. b'GET' from neutronclient's safe_encode_list) produces the literal string "b'GET'" instead of decoding to 'GET'. The fix is to normalize via the already-imported `to_native_string` (requests/utils.py), which decodes `bytes` to native str (utf-8) and leaves `str` untouched, preserving Python 2/3 behavior. Add a regression test next to test_unicode_method_name in test_requests.py asserting a bytes method is sent as 'GET'.

results.name: psf__requests-3362
results.summary: iter_content(decode_unicode=True) is NOT equivalent to Response.text. It delegates to stream_decode_response_unicode (requests/utils.py:359), which yields raw bytes unless r.encoding is set. Response.text, by contrast, falls back to chardet via apparent_encoding when self.encoding is None (requests/models.py:757-793). For an application/json response with no charset parameter, requests leaves encoding as None (only text/* content types get a default utf-8), so iter_content(decode_unicode=True) legitimately yields bytes. This is intended behavior, not a bug, so the smallest correct change is to clarify the Response.iter_content docstring (and optionally the helper/doc docs) rather than alter streaming semantics. Localization: the docstring is the primary change site; helper docstring and streaming docs are secondary.

results.name: psf__requests-1963
results.summary: In requests/sessions.py, `SessionRedirectMixin.resolve_redirects` rebuilds each hop from the original request: line 91 does `prepared_request = req.copy()` and line 102 does `method = req.method`. Because the base is always the initial request, a method change caused by an intermediate status (e.g. 303 See Other converting POST to GET) is not carried forward, so a later 307 re-sends the original POST instead of the intermediate GET. The fix is to track the request used for the previous hop (initialize `prepared_request = req` before the loop, then at the top of the loop copy the previous prepared request and derive `method` from it), while keeping 303/301/302 rewrites, 307/308 preservation, and cross-host Authorization stripping intact. A regression test should be added to `RequestsTestCase` in test_requests.py alongside the existing redirect tests (e.g. near test_cookie_sent_on_redirect / test_requests_in_history_are_not_overridden), covering the POST -> 303 -> 307 chain and asserting the final request method is GET.

results.name: pytest-dev__pytest-7432
results.summary: The reported behavior is caused by the `--runxfail` handling in `pytest_runtest_makereport` (src/_pytest/skipping.py). The branch `elif item.config.option.runxfail: pass  # don't interfere` (lines 273-274) sits before the marker-based skip fixup `elif item._store.get(skipped_by_mark_key, True) and rep.skipped and type(rep.longrepr) is tuple:` (lines 294-305). When --runxfail is set, that earlier branch wins for every outcome, so the fixup that rewrites `rep.longrepr` from the raise site within pytest to `item.reportinfo()` never runs; the raw `Skipped` tuple longrepr from `pytest_runtest_call`/`pytest_runtest_setup` is reported, yielding the src/_pytest/skipping.py location. The fix is to narrow/relocate the runxfail check so it only suppresses xfail conversion (the `xfail.Exception` and `xfailed` branches) and not the skip-location fixup, keeping XFAIL/XPASS and unittest unexpectedsuccess behavior intact.

results.name: django__django-14238
results.summary: The failure comes from AutoFieldMeta.__subclasscheck__ (django/db/models/fields/__init__.py), which currently only accepts the exact classes in the _subclasses tuple (BigAutoField, SmallAutoField) or direct AutoField subclasses. A user subclass of BigAutoField/SmallAutoField is neither in the tuple nor a real subclass of AutoField, so issubclass(pk_class, AutoField) in Options._get_default_pk_class fails with the ValueError. results.name: django__django-12915
results.summary: ASGIStaticFilesHandler inherits StaticFilesHandlerMixin, which only defines sync get_response(). StaticFilesHandlerMixin.load_middleware() is a no-op, so ASGIHandler._middleware_chain stays None and ASGIHandler.get_response_async -> base get_response_async calls self._middleware_chain(request), raising TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not callable. The fix is to add an async get_response_async coroutine to StaticFilesHandlerMixin (mirroring get_response: serve the static path, falling back to response_for_exception on Http404), using sync_to_async for the synchronous serve() call, so ASGIStaticFilesHandler inherits proper async static serving while StaticFilesHandler keeps its sync get_response override. Tests covering this should be added in tests/staticfiles_tests (new async handler test, plus url/helper fixtures for ASGI application).

results.name: matplotlib__matplotlib-25442
results.summary: Root cause: In `lib/matplotlib/offsetbox.py`, `DraggableBase.canvas` is defined as `property(lambda self: self.ref_artist.figure.canvas)`. When an artist (e.g. the AnnotationBbox ref_artist used by mplcursors) is removed from its figure during interaction, `ref_artist.figure` becomes `None`. `DraggableBase.on_release` calls `_check_still_parented()`, which sees `self.ref_artist.figure is None`, calls `self.disconnect()`, and `disconnect()` iterates `self.cids` calling `self.canvas.mpl_disconnect(cid)` — evaluating the `canvas` property on a None figure raises `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'canvas'`. The fix is to make `DraggableBase`/`AnnotationBbox` disconnect safely when the ref artist has lost its figure: guard the `canvas` property (return stored canvas or None), make `_check_still_parented`/`disconnect` tolerate a missing figure/canvas, and avoid storing the canvas lookup only via ref_artist (e.g. cache the canvas at connect time). Preserve existing behavior for valid, still-parented artists. A regression test reproducing the detached-ref_artist scenario belongs in lib/matplotlib/tests/test_offsetbox.py.

results.name: django__django-11001
results.summary: The bug is in django/db/models/sql/compiler.py. SQLCompiler.__init__ compiles self.ordering_parts = re.compile(r'(.*)\s(ASC|DESC)(.*)') without re.DOTALL/re.MULTILINE, so for multiline RawSQL order-by SQL the capture group (.*) matches only the final line, making distinct expressions with identical last lines look like duplicates. SQLCompiler.get_order_by uses that capture as the dedup key (without_ordering = self.ordering_parts.search(sql).group(1)), and SQLCompiler.get_extra_select uses the same extraction.
